meta.title: The one list
meta.authority: This file is the ONLY record of what is done. Prose docs explain the work; they do not track it.
meta.howToRead:
pnpm backlog          — the working view (open + blocked)
pnpm backlog --lane owner — one lane
pnpm check:backlog    — prove every row against the tree (runs in CI)
rules: A row's status is proven by its verify probe, not by memory. If they disagree, CI fails.
A probe must measure the CONSEQUENCE in the tree, never restate the row's own title. A probe that passes by existing is the shape-not-truth failure this repo names in four ADRs.
Manual rows never fail the build (ADR-970). They carry evidence + a checked date and go stale loudly.
Parked rows are not probed: 'you could do this now' is true of everything parked and therefore says nothing.
Never delete a probe to make CI pass. That is precisely how the previous five master lists drifted.

lanes.owner: Config or a decision. No code unblocks it.
lanes.program: A named multi-phase program. Needs a scheduling decision, not a start.
lanes.hygiene: Debt in the record or the instruments.

slate.note: The development order for the whole open queue, waves in sequence, ids in order within a wave. Owner-lane rows are decisions, not sequenced dev. Status lives only in each row’s probe; this object is the sequence.

W3 · Loom foundation (the media layer the editor projects from)
W4 · the Editor, E0-E9 in order (decision gate first: EDITOR-ARCHITECTURE’s two open sequencing questions)

slate.rationale: Foundation before surface: hardening and module boundaries (A1/A3) pay compounding dividends across every later wave. Loom D1-D3 precede the Editor because E2 projects the editor’s asset model onto the Loom. Content retirements (W1) must precede E3, which replaces EDITABLE_PAGES in the opposite direction. Re-theme and the DAWN mechanical sweeps follow the editor so swept surfaces are not rebuilt. Flagship apps (A4) and the domain backlog ride after boundaries + editor exist. Commerce verticals close, with Resonance’s launch GO still the owner’s. White label (E10/W6/P7), mobile, and texting park by name.

entries.title: check:adoption stays advisory (owner decision), and the other two checks were already required

source.ref: §5 the constraint that governs the plan

entries.detail: CLOSED 2026-08-18 by an owner decision, after the row rescoped from three clicks to one question. 🔴 CORRECTED 2026-08-18, SAME DAY, BY OBSERVATION. This row was closed claiming TWO of the three were already done. Only ONE was. check:contrast genuinely blocks - it sits in ci.yml's guards array inside the checks job, so requiring it separately would be a second name for the same gate. THE pr-compare CLAIM WAS FALSE, and it was taken from prose: .github/workflows/pr-compare-fallback.yml asserts in its first line that pr-compare is a REQUIRED status context, citing ruleset 17640795. PR #2161 disproved it by merging. Auto-merge fired at 21:45:31 while the pr-compare check run was still in_progress (it completed success at 21:52:50), and the merged SHA carried exactly one commit status, Vercel's - so no substitute pr-compare status stood in for it. A context that is required cannot be pending at merge. See LIVE-049. The irony is the point: this row was closed by citing a sentence in a file, hours after ADR-1082 made 're-test the premise, do not trust the prose' a rule in AGENTS.md. THE THIRD WAS A DECISION, NOT A TASK, and the owner made it: check:adoption STAYS ADVISORY. ci.yml's own twenty-line rationale carried the argument (ADR-970): it is a SCOREBOARD of design-debt COUNTS, a count ratchet fires on legitimate growth - 'bespoke-cards: 0 means adding any new *-card.tsx fails a PR that has nothing to do with the design system' - and an advisory finding forced through a blocking gate teaches everyone to route around the gate. THE COST OF THAT CHOICE IS KNOWN AND ACCEPTED, and is written here so the next reader does not have to rediscover it: literal-radius read '🔴 rose' from 2026-08-13 to 2026-08-18 and nobody looked, even though the advisory step already writes the scoreboard into every run's summary. The gate is visible and was still unread; that is an argument about ATTENTION, not about blocking, and the remedy if it recurs is a louder surface (a PR comment rather than a run summary), not a reversal of this decision. Re-open only with new evidence, not with the same argument.

verify.evidence: pr-compare: ruleset 17640795 was READ by the owner on 2026-08-18 and the required set is checks + analyze + lint + test + Vercel. pr-compare is not required; the earlier evidence on this row cited .github/workflows/pr-compare-fallback.yml line 1 instead of the ruleset, and that sentence was wrong. See LIVE-049. check:contrast: ci.yml guards array, line 262. check:adoption: ci.yml 'Advisory trackers (reported, never blocking)', continue-on-error: true - the owner confirmed on 2026-08-18 that this stays as it is.

entries.title: Upgrade Healthchecks.io so all 27 crons are monitored
entries.detail:

Also set each check's period from the real schedule: auto-created checks arrive at 1 day, so process-queue (every 2 min) could be dead most of a day before anyone is paged.

Whether the account was upgraded is NOT readable here, and the reason is structural rather than an oversight: lib/observability/cron-heartbeat.ts:41-51 makes the ping a safe no-op when CRON_HEARTBEAT_BASE_URL is unset, so an unconfigured base and a full-but-capped account look identical from inside the repo. scripts/cron-freshness.mjs:492 says so itself. Settled by the Healthchecks.io project page showing plan and check count.

entries.title: White on amber STAYS: letterpress the primary label - chiseled white, dark edge, sunken into the button
entries.detail:
OWNER DECISION 2026-08-19, verbatim: "Figure out how to change the rules or clean this up so I can have white on amber. The ideal would be chisel/embossed white with a little dark edge. Giving the effect that it's sunken into the button." That RESOLVES the two-option question this row used to carry (darken the label vs darken the fill): the answer is NEITHER. The white label and the brand amber both stay, and the label renders as a LETTERPRESS. Implemented in .text-emboss (app/globals.css): a crisp 1px ring of --brand-emboss-dark on all four sides of each glyph, the two upper diagonals doubled (sunken = darkest along the top wall), a 1.5px-blur occlusion into the cavity top, and a 1.5px --brand-emboss-light catch-light below as the lit lower lip. Applied through the variant seams only: components/ui/button.tsx (primary now carries text-emboss beside chisel) and components/marketing/marketing-ui.tsx (primary already carried it). MEASURED 2026-08-19 (axe-core 4.13.0, real headless chromium; jsdom cannot evaluate color-contrast, see test/a11y/axe.ts): axe credits a same-colour ZERO-BLUR text-shadow group covering all four glyph edges (each offset > 0.5px) as a text STROKE and measures the label against ring-over-fill instead of the bare amber. White on all four brand ambers moved from VIOLATION (2.52 / 1.87 / 2.86 / 1.94:1) to PASS (15.2-19.8:1 as axe reports the composited ground), at both button type sizes. A blurred shadow alone can never do this (axe discounts its alpha by 0.185/(blur/em+0.4) and it covers at most one edge), which is why the OLD two-shadow emboss was measured, failed, and waived. WHAT THE PROBE WAITS ON: a real CI @a11y capture confirming the flip on live surfaces, which re-freezes a11y-baselines.json (the eight midnight-dark contexts should drop) and retires the six now-unmatched fgOnShadowColor waiver entries in test/e2e/a11y-waivers.ts. The FILL waivers stay: pills/badges/toggles still paint white on amber without the letterpress, and the token pair itself is unchanged (2.52:1 etc., frozen in scripts/check-contrast.mjs - the letterpress changes what axe measures on buttons, not what the palette declares). Visual baselines need a recapture: every primary button renders differently.

── CLOSED 2026-08-20: the CI capture ran (e2e-manual on PR #2196, against the emboss preview). The a11y re-freeze wrote the wins down: /discover midnight-dark 2 → 0 and /pricing midnight-dark 1 → 0, zero serious+ violations in every captured context. The six fgOnShadowColor waiver entries for the old two-shadow emboss retired in the same change (axe no longer reports those composites; the guard inverted to assert NO shadow-keyed entries remain). Visual recapture committed. The FILL waivers stay: pills, badges and toggles still paint white on amber without the letterpress.

verify.cmd: node -e 'const fs=require("fs");const css=fs.readFileSync("app/globals.css","utf8");const m=css.match(/\.text-emboss\s*\{[^}]*\}/);const ring=!!m&&["0 -1px 0","1px 0 0","-1px 0 0","0 1px 0"].every(o=>m[0].includes(o+" var(--brand-emboss-dark)"));const btn=fs.readFileSync("components/ui/button.tsx","utf8").includes("text-emboss");const captured=!fs.readFileSync("test/e2e/a11y-waivers.ts","utf8").includes("#bf7a28");process.exit(ring&&btn&&captured?0:1)'

entries.notes: HISTORY. Opened as an owner DECISION row (two measured remedies: ink-on-amber 7.90:1, or a real midnight-dark primary-strong 7.46:1). 2026-08-18: owner said WAIVE FOR NOW; the eight midnight-dark contexts were carried in a11y-baselines.json and the row sat blocked. 2026-08-19: owner picked a third direction nobody had offered - keep white on amber and cut it INTO the button - which turned the decision row into this implementation row. The probe passes only when (a) the four-sided --brand-emboss-dark ring exists in .text-emboss, (b) components/ui/button.tsx primary carries text-emboss, and (c) the stale fgOnShadowColor waiver composites (#bf7a28 et al) are gone from test/e2e/a11y-waivers.ts - (c) is the CI capture confirming on live pages what the local chromium measurement showed, so the row cannot close on a local prediction.

entries.title: Rule the access='space_members' semantics: relabel (A), widen the predicate (B), or add a mode (C)
entries.detail:
OWNER RULING 2026-08-20, verbatim: "C: add a paid mode". access='space_members' KEEPS staff semantics and its copy stops promising paying members (label 'Space team only'); a new sixth mode space_paid_members admits ACTIVE space_memberships holders (label 'Space members only', the sentence the old mode wrongly promised). Implemented per ADR-1092: supabase/migrations/20270319000000_circle_space_paid_members.sql (six-value CHECK, private.is_space_paid_member, can_enter_circle arm flip, is_space_audience dropped, trigger learns the mode), lib/circles/visibility.ts + space-entry.ts + store.ts + app/(main)/circles/actions.ts, help article, pgTAP supabase/tests/circle_space_paid_members.test.sql.

── PREMISE CORRECTION (the ADR-1082 pattern, found while working the row): this row and CIRCLES-C3-PLAN §4.2 said the mode reads the staff ladder at BOTH layers. The DB layer had NOT been staff-only since ADR-1021 applied (2026-08-12): live can_enter_circle asked private.is_space_audience = staff OR active paid membership, i.e. option B's substance was already in production. Ruling C therefore also NARROWS space_members back to staff. Measured live impact of the narrowing: nil — 7 circles, all access='open', 0 closed (2026-08-20).

entries.title: Config and env: the remaining unset keys (three of the six were already set)
entries.detail:
🔴 RE-MEASURED 2026-08-19 AND THE ROW WAS WRONG ABOUT HALF ITS OWN CONTENTS. Three of the six items were already satisfied, and the row had been telling the owner to go and do them. The previous evidence line said the rest are "Vercel/Resend dashboard state, not readable here", which is the exact shape ADR-1082 names: a blocker phrased as "cannot be checked" is a claim with an expiry date. The SECRET is unreadable from an agent container. Its CONSEQUENCE is sitting in the database.

ALREADY DONE, do not spend anything on these:
  • Supabase -> Pro. The organization (hkveprznovcteywuczcv) returns plan "pro". Capacity and     backups are on the paid tier already.
  • RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET. Email metrics are NOT dark. public.email_events over the trailing 30     days holds opened=127, delivered=81 and clicked=3. Those three event types cannot be produced     by our own send path -- nothing server-side knows an email was opened -- so they can only have     arrived through the Resend webhook, which means the secret is set AND the signature check is     passing. Most recent delivered event 2026-08-19T13:04:20Z, i.e. the same day this was measured.
  • VAPID, the PUBLIC half. public.push_subscriptions holds 23 rows, 8 of them created in the last     30 days, most recent 2026-08-10. A browser cannot complete pushManager.subscribe() without     NEXT_PUBLIC_VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY being served to it, so that key is live and members have been     granting permission for two months.

STILL GENUINELY OPEN:
  • VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY, the SEND half. Subscriptions prove the public key, not the private one.     lib/push.ts:22 warns '[push] VAPID keys not set - push sending disabled.' and returns false     when either key is missing, so the cheap settling move is a runtime-log search for that exact     string rather than another dashboard trip. Note the queue is quiet (1 notification_queue row in     24h), so absence of the warning in a short retention window is not proof either way -- it needs     a window that contains an actual push attempt.
  • Verify frequencylocal.com in Resend, plus SPF/DKIM/DMARC subdomain isolation. Blocking for     volume. The delivered events above prove sending works TODAY at current volume; they say     nothing about domain reputation at scale, which is what this item is for.
  • Secret-scanning push protection.
  • Dismiss the 3 CodeQL false positives.

CRON_SECRET and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY remain satisfied by consequence: ai_usage holds 50 rows in the trailing 7 days, and the crons are firing.

entries.title: Lift 8b: a loading prop on IconButton, matching Button's
entries.detail: Icon-only controls are exactly the ones where a tap leaves no other evidence it landed.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const S='components/ui/icon-button.tsx',T='components/ui/icon-button.test.tsx';if(!fs.existsSync(S)||!fs.existsSync(T))process.exit(79);const src=fs.readFileSync(S,'utf8'),test=fs.readFileSync(T,'utf8');const cut=src.indexOf('export function IconLink');if(cut<0)process.exit(79);const B=src.slice(0,cut),L=src.slice(cut);function a(s,k){let i=0;while((i=s.indexOf(k+'={',i))>=0){const aria=s.slice(Math.max(0,i-5),i).endsWith('aria-');const e=s.indexOf('}',i);if(e>0&&s.slice(i,e).includes('loading')&&(k.indexOf('aria-')===0||!aria))return true;i+=k.length}return false}const bad=[];if(!a(B,'disabled'))bad.push('IconButton does not disable while loading; a second tap re-fires the action');if(!a(B,'aria-busy'))bad.push('IconButton does not set aria-busy while loading');if(!a(L,'aria-disabled'))bad.push('IconLink does not set aria-disabled while loading');if(!a(L,'aria-busy'))bad.push('IconLink does not set aria-busy while loading');if(!test.includes('does not fire the handler again'))bad.push('the double-fire assertion is gone from '+T);if(bad.length){console.error(bad.join('; '));process.exit(1)}process.exit(0)"

entries.notes: Closed 2026-08-17. The probe that flagged this row as stale was `grep-present /loading/` in the component, which passes because the WORD appears anywhere in the file, including in a comment describing the prop it is supposed to be proving. Replaced with the consequence: IconButton must disable while loading (so a second tap cannot re-fire the action) and set aria-busy; IconLink must use the aria pair INSTEAD of the real `disabled`, because a real disabled drops it out of the tab order mid-navigation; and the double-fire assertion must still exist in the test file. ONE TRAP WORTH RECORDING: both controls live in one file and the string 'aria-disabled=' CONTAINS 'disabled=', so an unscoped regex let each component satisfy the other's check. Two of four deliberate breaks passed before that was caught, which is exactly why a probe is not trusted until it has been seen to fail. It now splits the file at IconLink and judges each half alone; all four breaks fire. A SECOND trap cost another round: the first scoped version used a regex, and this string travels JSON -> shell -> `node -e`, where a lone backslash does not survive intact - "\\b" arrived as a literal BACKSPACE, so every check silently matched nothing and the row read as regressed. The probe is now backslash-free, scanning with indexOf instead of RegExp, and was re-proved through the guard's own shell rather than only standalone.

entries.title: Lift 8b: an in-flight cue on DirectorySearch
entries.detail: It fetches. Until it says so, an empty result and a pending one look identical.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const S='components/ui/directory-search.tsx',T='components/ui/directory-search.test.tsx';if(!fs.existsSync(S)||!fs.existsSync(T))process.exit(79);const s=fs.readFileSync(S,'utf8'),t=fs.readFileSync(T,'utf8');const code=s.split(String.fromCharCode(10)).filter(x=>x.trim().indexOf('//')!==0&&x.trim().indexOf('*')!==0).join(String.fromCharCode(10));const bad=[];if(code.indexOf('useTransition()')<0)bad.push('DirectorySearch does not CALL useTransition(), so it cannot know a search is in flight');const i=code.indexOf('aria-busy={');const seg=i<0?'':code.slice(i,code.indexOf('}',i));if(i<0||seg.indexOf('isPending')<0)bad.push('aria-busy is not driven by isPending');if(code.indexOf('Searching')<0)bad.push('the live-region text is gone; a spinning glyph announces nothing to a screen reader');if((t.split('expect(').length-1)<3)bad.push('fewer than 3 assertions in '+T);if(bad.length){console.error(bad.join('; '));process.exit(1)}process.exit(0)"

entries.notes: Closed 2026-08-17. Was manual pending the implementation. The probe requires useTransition to be CALLED, not merely imported: the first version matched the token and passed while the component tracked nothing, because the import line alone satisfied it. entries.notes: Closed 2026-08-17. 42 primitives, 6 carry a state test, 36 grandfathered in scripts/ui-state-test-ledger.txt — a SET of paths, not a count, because one primitive gaining a test and one arriving without cancel out inside a total (the ADR-1007 defect). The definition of 'state test' is INTERACTION-STATES.md's, not invented: names 3+ of the nine states in test titles, titles only — exercising a state in a className assertion is not naming it. 36 is not 36 units of neglect: a Display badge owes only `rest`, so the gate over-reports by design and can never certify an untested primitive as covered. entries.title: The .dark [data-skin="midnight"] selector never matches on the <html> path
entries.detail: A descendant combinator cannot match an element against itself. app/layout.tsx stamps data-skin on documentElement (the global skin preview path, including marketing); only the shell root is a descendant. So midnight-dark renders a MIXTURE: the generic .dark palette with midnight's light-mode overrides under it. The comment at app/layout.tsx:142-143 asserts the opposite, which is why it survived. One selector, but it repaints every midnight-dark surface, so it wants its own pass with a baseline recapture.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const S='lib/theme/skins.ts',C='app/globals.css';if(!fs.existsSync(S)||!fs.existsSync(C))process.exit(79);const src=fs.readFileSync(S,'utf8');const ids=[...new Set([...src.matchAll(/\bid:\s*\x27([a-z0-9-]+)\x27/g)].map(m=>m[1]))];const def=(src.match(/DEFAULT_SKIN[^=]*=\s*\x27([a-z0-9-]+)\x27/)||[])[1];if(!def||ids.length<2)process.exit(79);const css=fs.readFileSync(C,'utf8').replace(/\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\//g,'');const bad=[];for(const id of ids){if(id===def)continue;if(!new RegExp('\\\\.dark\\\\[data-skin=\\\\x22'+id+'\\\\x22\\\\]').test(css))bad.push(id+': no compound .dark[data-skin] selector; the <html> preview path paints the generic .dark palette');if(!new RegExp('\\\\.dark\\\\s+\\\\[data-skin=\\\\x22'+id+'\\\\x22\\\\]').test(css))bad.push(id+': no descendant .dark [data-skin] selector; the authed-shell path loses its dark block');}if(bad.length){console.error(bad.join('\n'));process.exit(1)}process.exit(0)"

entries.notes: Closed 2026-08-17. Non-vacuity proven by the parent, not taken on report: reverting to the descendant-only selector fails skin-dom-selectors.test.ts with 'A descendant combinator cannot match an element against itself'. The second half matters more than the row did — authoring the selector LIST would have silently dropped the block from check-contrast's resolver, which scored the raw prelude and returned null for any comma-separated selector, so the contrast gate would have kept printing green for midnight-dark while measuring nothing there (ADR-970). Fixed in the same pass; selectorWeight now scores each part of a list independently.

entries.title: The app shell statically imports the entire admin module registry
entries.detail: settings-panel.tsx imports MODULE_COMPONENTS from components/admin/modules/module-map — a 'use client' pure registry with 38 static imports and no hooks, handlers or browser APIs. It reaches crypto-browserify/stream-browserify: 406 kB raw / 121 kB gzip on EVERY authed page, verified as a blocking script tag in served HTML. Fix: next/dynamic per module, import module IDS not components, and add import 'server-only' to lib/journey-plans and lib/practices so the class fails the build. (2) THE crypto-browserify HALF WAS REAL, and it was NOT in module-map. entries.title: Sentry no longer ships to routes with no DSN configured
entries.detail: The static `import * as Sentry` is gone; the SDK is now reached through a dynamic import gated on process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN — the one env form the browser can resolve, since Next inlines NEXT_PUBLIC_* at build time. The server-only SENTRY_DSN fallback is deliberately NOT consulted here because it is never inlined into the browser bundle and could only read undefined. The hard part was the export contract: Next reads onRouterTransitionStart off this module's namespace and calls it on every client navigation, so it MUST stay defined with Sentry off — it is now a stable wrapper delegating to an async-loaded hook, with a .catch that leaves it a no-op if the chunk fails, because monitoring must never take down the app it monitors. Stated cost: a navigation in the first few ms of a configured session may go untraced. VERIFIED BEYOND THE ONE FILE (the searchSiteIcons lesson): every importer of lib/observability/sentry was enumerated — only sentry.server.config.ts and sentry.edge.config.ts import it statically, both server/edge runtimes, and lib/maps/diagnostics.ts deliberately reads the value without importing. No client component pulls it, so the SDK cannot re-enter the baseline chunk by a side door.
entries.notes: Artifact-verified 2026-08-17, not inferred: built with no DSN and read the emitted chunks. The 236,682-byte Sentry SDK chunk appears in 0 of 4,149 client entry lists across all 404 page_client-reference-manifest.js files, and the baseline chunk in rootMainFiles contains only the gated async loader. app/error, app/global-error and components/ui/route-error.tsx still import the SDK statically; Turbopack keeps those in async groups, so they are not a baseline regression and were deliberately left alone.

source.ref: ADR-1080; docs/FINALIZE-PLAN.md 10.9, 10.12; proxy.ts next= carry from #2132

entries.title: The sitemap's batched podcast read was silently truncating at 1000 rows
entries.detail: THE ROW'S PREMISE WAS STALE AND THE REAL BUG WAS WORSE. The N+1 had already been collapsed — sitemap.ts called a batched reader. But that batch used `.limit(min(n*200, 5000))` with no `.range()`, and `.limit()` does not raise PostgREST's server-side `max_rows` (supabase/config.toml:18 = 1000, and service_role does not escape it). So it declared a 5000-row appetite, received 1000, and reported no error. Because the batch orders `created_at DESC` ACROSS ALL SPACES, the dropped rows were whole trailing Spaces: their /podcasts index and every Show URL vanished from the sitemap with nothing to notice. Collapsing 200 correct small queries into one truncated one traded latency for missing URLs — the third instance today of a fix whose instrument could not tell 'nothing there' from 'I could not see'. Now paged explicitly with `.range()` over a TOTAL order (created_at DESC, id ASC — the tiebreaker is required so a created_at tie cannot straddle a page boundary and be skipped or repeated), stopping on a short page. Still O(rows), never O(Spaces).

verify.note: Probes the CONSEQUENCE — that the batched read pages — rather than the row's words. Backed by app/sitemap.test.ts, which rebuilds the URL list the old per-Space loop would have emitted and requires an exact match, and which was confirmed to FAIL against an unpaged read (expected 1000 to be 1500) before being accepted.

entries.title: Build a function-grant guard
entries.detail: There is no repo-side gate for function grants at all: check-grants.mjs covers tables only, and nothing anywhere references has_function_privilege. 29 anon-executable SECURITY DEFINER functions currently rest on a human remembering to read an advisor. entries.notes: Closed 2026-08-17. The row's ORIGINAL probe was grep-present /has_function_privilege/ in scripts — shape-not-truth, and it proved it: the moment the new guard file appeared it passed by the string existing, and check:backlog correctly failed the row as stale within minutes. IT READS supabase/migrations/, NOT THE DATABASE, and says so in its own output: prod still held 29 anon- and 49 authenticated-executable SECURITY DEFINER functions when last measured. This guard holds the line; OWN-006 is the sweep that closes the gap.

entries.title: R7: the eyebrow role is no longer hand-rolled where the code itself names it
entries.detail: THE ROW'S PREMISE WAS WRONG AND THE MEASUREMENT SAYS SO. It called this 'largely mechanical' over ~698 sites with 3 adopters. entries.notes: Closed 2026-08-17 (ADR-1071). THE ROW WAS STALE ON THE IMPLEMENTATION AND RIGHT ABOUT THE GAP. The three-position ladder and the desktop left-rail fold were already built and already gated. The PERSISTED half had nothing behind it: replacing the whole body of writeStoredRailFolds with `return` left all 38 tests in rail-fold.test.ts PASSING, and deleting railFold from the shell mount in app/(main)/layout.tsx - the entire no-flash path - left 288 tests passing with tsc green. Cause: that suite runs in environment 'node', so with no window and no document both storage functions return on their first line in every case. AND IT SURFACED A REAL DEFECT. writeStoredRailFolds is built to survive blocked localStorage (the setItem throw is swallowed, the cookie still lands) but readStoredRailFolds read localStorage and nothing else. In exactly that case the server paints the folded strip from the cookie, hydration renders it, and the first client snapshot reads blocked storage, answers Auto, and shoves the rail open one frame after paint - the fail-safe fired and the next line cancelled it. The read now falls back to the cookie. The probe EXECUTES the round trip rather than grepping for it: it fakes window.localStorage and document.cookie, chooses Strip/Open, drops the in-memory snapshot (a reload) and asserts the fold comes back AND that the cookie the server reads agrees. Verified myself, not just reported: gutting the write prints 'a reload lost the fold' and exits 1; removing compact={leftStrip} names the desktop fold and exits 1. No baseline recapture needed - the rail's state at rest is unchanged, and the new behaviour only fires when localStorage is empty AND a cookie exists, which a fresh capture browser never has.

entries.title: Nothing prevents the build cache overflowing again, because the gate that would is calibrated in the wrong units
entries.detail:
RE-MEASURED 2026-08-18, and the row changed shape rather than closing. THE SYMPTOM IS GONE: three consecutive production builds (18:46, 19:01, 19:09) uploaded 1.26 / 1.28 / 1.29 GB against the 1.50 GB ceiling and every one logged 'Restored build cache from previous deployment'. No invalidation line anywhere. The 1.53 GB reading the row was filed on does not reproduce. WHAT IS STILL TRUE is the second half of the original row: nothing PREVENTS a recurrence. scripts/check-cache-budget.mjs was written for exactly that on 2026-08-17 and has never run on a real build. It was wired into postbuild in #2159 and TAKEN BACK OUT before merge, because the preview build of that change printed what no amount of reading could: 'TRIMMED the build cache before Vercel could reject it. What the build was about to hand back measured 2.40 GiB, over the 1.38 GiB trim point. drops the cheap half instead: .next/cache/turbopack (1520 MiB).' THE FLOOR ARM WAS RIGHT (node_modules 933 MiB, 27% clear of its 1.25 GiB budget, exactly as predicted). THE TRIM ARM IS CALIBRATED AGAINST THE WRONG QUANTITY: measure() sums RAW BYTES ON DISK and Vercel's ceiling applies to the PACKED archive. Raw 2.40 GiB versus a packed upload of 1.26-1.29 GB is about 2:1, not the ~3% the script's header assumes, because the Turbopack cache compresses hard and is the dominant term. Wired as-is it would delete a 1.5 GiB compiler cache on EVERY build to prevent an overflow that is not happening, turning a working warm cache into a guaranteed cold compile forever. TO CLOSE: fix the calibration (LIVE-048), then wire the gate in the SAME change as a preview build that prints it green. Do NOT close this row by deleting the guard or by declaring the symptom gone: the symptom being gone is why there is time to get the instrument right, not a reason to skip it.

STILL OPEN 2026-08-19, and the reason is now narrower than 'the gate is broken'. The gate is fixed (LIVE-048) and it is running on every production build, but in WARN-ONLY mode (LIVE-035): it measures and reports and cannot trim. So a cache heading for the 1.50 GB ceiling would be SEEN and named in the build log, and then nothing would stop it. Recurrence is now visible rather than prevented, which is a real improvement over nothing watching and is still not this row. It closes when the gate is promoted to blocking on the strength of a confirmed PACKED_PER_RAW.

Trend, read from production build logs on 2026-08-19: packed cache uploads of 1.26 GB across the day's deploys against the 1.50 GB ceiling, consistent with the 1.26 / 1.28 / 1.29 GB readings from 2026-08-18. Not rising.

THE PROBE ON THIS ROW WAS ITSELF WRONG, and the tree caught it the same day. It asked only whether check-cache-budget appears in postbuild. On 2026-08-19 it started appearing there in --warn-only mode, so the probe flipped to passing while the row stayed true: nothing prevents an overflow, it is merely reported now. That is the shape-not-truth failure four ADRs name, and a probe walked into it the first time the tree moved. Rewritten to measure the CONSEQUENCE -- the gate must be in postbuild AND not carry --warn-only AND still contain a delete path -- so it agrees with the row today and passes only when an overflow can actually be stopped.

HEADROOM RE-READ 2026-08-19 with the corrected constant, and it is tighter than this row assumed. Preview build 3jeNVZxuUy7thPjXpazjMC6yHwVo uploaded 1.32 GB against the 1.50 GB ceiling: 12% clear, not the 16% the 1.26 GB production reads implied. The cache is a single term, turbopack at 1459 MiB, so there is no second thing to trim if it grows. The gate now SEES this on every build and still cannot act on it.

🔴 FOUR PACKED READINGS TODAY, AND THE HEADROOM IS NARROWING:
    2026-08-18 production          1.26 GB   16% clear
    2026-08-19 production          1.26 GB   16% clear
    2026-08-19 preview (#2178)     1.32 GB   12% clear
    2026-08-19 preview (#2179)     1.35 GB   10% clear

⚠️ READ THAT CAREFULLY RATHER THAN AS A TREND LINE. The two production builds started COLD ('Build cache: <1 MB' on input), while the two previews compiled against a warm turbopack cache, so the 1.26 and the 1.35 are not the same measurement repeated. What IS comparable is the two previews, 8 minutes apart: turbopack went 1459 -> 1493 MiB, and those trees differed in what they compiled, so even that is one observation and not a rate.

What is NOT in doubt is the tightest true reading: 1.35 GB against a 1.50 GB ceiling is 10% clear, on a cache whose .next/cache half is a SINGLE term. If turbopack grows past roughly 1.65 GiB the whole cache is discarded, node_modules included, and the gate that would trim it first is deliberately unable to (warn-only, LIVE-035). That is this row, stated in numbers.

SIXTH READING, and it widens rather than tightens: preview xpkMNeSxJCWTTn35uvCeoacVbM7n uploaded 1.29 GB, 14% clear. The 8.7%-clear production figure from dpl_6FfMfAv7mHXQ3P2X3GmTxSCwDvEz remains the MAXIMUM observed and is still the number to plan against -- a preview that compiled less code is not evidence the ceiling moved. Recorded because the spread between same-day builds (1.26-1.37 GB) is now visibly dominated by what each build compiled, which is the reason this row still refuses to call any of it a trend line.

entries.title: 20 route handlers are green by human assertion, and 11 of them claim `public`
entries.detail: check:authz now sees all 72 route handlers, but 52 are green because a gate was DETECTED and 20 because a human read them and said so. The ledger states this in its own header rather than hiding it, and pins each route's normalized-body digest so an edit forces a re-read — but a reason is not a proof. The sharp end is the three asserted `public` routes that touch the admin client: app/api/vitals, app/api/people/[handle]/vcard, app/api/llms.txt. Give each a per-route test pinning what it must never return, the way app/api/status/route.test.ts already pins its 'no secret' promise. That converts the highest-risk assertions into verifications and leaves the genuinely-trivial ones asserted.

entries.title: check:authz is file-level: it sees a gate is called, not that it runs on every path
entries.detail: LIVE-022 closed the VISIBILITY half — app/api/** was invisible because the classifier's first predicate required 'use server', which a Next 16 Route Handler never is. The granularity half is untouched and the guard's own header says so: it detects that a recognised gate is called SOMEWHERE in the file, not that it runs before every write on every path through every exported method. A route exporting GET and POST where only GET is gated reads as green. Stated here rather than left in an agent report, because an unrecorded limitation is how a partial gate comes to be read as full coverage (ADR-970).

verify.evidence: scripts/check-authz-guards.mjs header states the file-level limit explicitly. Confirmed 2026-08-17: the classifier tests src for gate tokens per FILE, with no per-export analysis.

entries.notes: Closed 2026-08-17 (ADR-1070). check:authz was FILE-level: it saw a gate called somewhere in the file, so an early return before the gate, a gate on one branch of an if, and a gated GET beside an ungated POST all read as green. It now requires EVERY exported HTTP method to pass three structural rules, following the body through a wrapper's local handler (27 cron routes) and into file-local helpers: R1 per-export, R2 the gate is not nested inside if/else/switch/catch, R3 no createAdminClient() query above the gate. R3 IS A DELIBERATE NARROWING AND THE MEASUREMENT IS WHY. A literal 'any return before the gate' rule was tried against the real corpus first: it fires on 10 of the 52 gated handlers and all ten are validation (400 on a malformed body, 429 on rate limit, an empty list for a blank query). Shipping that would have been 100% false positives on day one, which is the ADR-970 shape - a guard that cannot fire honestly gets routed around and then reads as coverage. What is dangerous is not returning early, it is answering from the service-role client before you know who is asking, and that is what R3 measures. IT FOUND THREE REAL FALSE GREENS, each re-verdicted as a digest-pinned human reading: check-handle (auth.getUser inside an if, over a SECURITY DEFINER RPC) -> public; auth/callback (auth.getUser three branches deep in a swallowed analytics block; the real credential check is exchangeCodeForSession) -> token-credential; q/[slug] (service-role read of the code row before getMyProfileId, which answers WHO scanned, not MAY they) -> self-scoped. Counts moved 52 gated / 20 asserted to 49 / 23, and the standing 'the ledger must never outgrow the gated set' test still holds.

entries.title: check:backlog costs 24s and grows ~2s per closed row, because ten probes each spawn a vitest run
entries.detail: MEASURED, not estimated: `node scripts/check-backlog.mjs` takes 23.9s. 21 rows carry a cmd probe and TEN of them spawn a full vitest run to prove their consequence — the honest instrument, and an expensive one. It already turned CI red once: backlog-contract.test.ts's ripgrep-parity arm runs the guard TWICE by design and blew the default 30s test timeout. That is patched with a raised timeout and a comment, which treats the symptom; the number comes back at roughly +2s per row closed the same way, and 39 rows are still open. It is also duplicated work: those test files already run in `pnpm test`, so the probe re-runs what CI just ran. Options worth weighing, none obviously right: a probe protocol where the row names a test file and the guard trusts the suite to have run it (loses standalone verifiability, which is the whole point); running the vitest probes in one batched invocation instead of ten; or a --only-static mode for the parity arm, whose property is about the SEARCH engine and does not need the cmd probes at all. Do NOT solve it by making probes cheaper in a way that stops them measuring the consequence — that is the failure this backlog exists to prevent.

entries.notes: Re-measured 2026-08-17, after the ten suite-spawning probes were rewritten to measure the same consequence in-process: the guard costs 6.2s, down from 23.1s on the same tree with the same clock. What is left, in order: PROG-DAWN9 2.8s, LIVE-014 1.2s (it runs check-labels.mjs over the whole tsx tree), every other probe under 350ms. THE PROBE BELOW USED TO TIME THE GUARD BY RUNNING THE GUARD, and that was wrong twice over. It was a FORK BOMB: the child ran this same probe, which spawned another child, without end; 55 live processes were counted on 2026-08-17, each orphaned chain outliving the run that started it. That, not the vitest spawns, is why backlog-contract.test.ts still timed out after its limit was raised to 240s. And even fenced against re-entry it doubled every invocation forever: 6.2s of probe work cost 12.5s of wall clock, here and in CI. So the row now probes the CAUSE instead — no verify.cmd may spawn a test runner — which costs milliseconds and cannot re-enter. The row cannot police itself, so its own id is excluded from that scan; a floor of 15 cmd probes makes an unreadable or reshaped file exit 79 rather than report a clean sweep of nothing. The WALL-CLOCK ceiling did not disappear with the timing probe: it moved to backlog-contract.test.ts's ripgrep-parity arm, which already runs the guard twice by design and now fails if either run exceeds 20s. Cause measured for free on every probe run, consequence measured for free in the suite that was paying for it anyway.

entries.title: The "Founding Business offer" email promises a rate that no longer exists
entries.detail:
FOUNDING_BUSINESS (lib/beta/launch-emails.ts, mirrored in lib/beta/email-templates.ts) is seeded into Email Studio as a campaign offering local businesses "A Founding Business gets its own Space to post events and offers and the lowest rate we will ever set, kept for good. Take the year before September 1". ADR-1067 removed the Business founding rate, so there is no price behind that promise: Business is a flat $29/mo, $290/yr, and the only beta rate in the catalog is Collective's unlisted $49/$490. Nothing is mis-sold TODAY because these are seeded drafts rather than sends, and the campaign links to /pricing rather than to a checkout at a named rate. But if it goes out as written it offers a founding rate the catalog cannot charge. Owner decides which: retire the email, or repoint the offer at Collective (whose rate IS grantable, and whose September 1 framing already matches). The badge and Space copy are reusable either way. NOT a code fix to guess at - the email is an offer, and which offer to make is the owner's call.

── 2026-08-19, AND THIS ROW'S CLOSE WAS INCOMPLETE. It was scoped to lib/beta/launch-emails.ts and lib/beta/email-templates.ts, and the exact sentence it reported removing was alive VERBATIM in a third file the close never looked at: lib/email-studio/presets.ts, in a preset named FOUNDING_BUSINESS_INVITE ('the lowest rate we will ever set, kept for good'). Its probe could never have caught it, because both files it read are now deleted and it returns indeterminate. The copy is fixed and the probe re-pointed at the file that actually carries the offer. The lesson is the row's own: a close scoped to the files you happened to grep is not a close, and the mitigation everyone reached for (nothing imports EMAIL_PRESETS outside its test) is the same dormancy this row judged unacceptable when it was filed.

FOUNDING_BUSINESS is out of BETA_LAUNCH_EMAILS (so the seeder never writes it into `campaigns`) and the matching plain-text template is out of email-templates.ts. The constant is KEPT and exported as RETIRED_FOUNDING_BUSINESS_EMAIL: the Founding Business PROGRAM - badge, 25-per-city cap, take-rate buy-down - is recognition rather than a discount and is not retired, so the copy stays available to rewrite without a founding RATE in it. entries.title: A SECOND path can still stamp a lifetime $19 on a Founding Business, and it is not the catalog
entries.detail: ADR-1067 removed the Business founding rate from the CATALOG, which is what the Stripe sync mints from. It does NOT touch FOUNDING_DEFAULT.business_monthly_cents in lib/pricing/founding.ts, still 1900. That constant is live on a different path: the beta founder push (ADR-875, tightened by ADR-880) runs space-subscriptions.ts -> beta-founding.ts -> grantFoundingStatus, which stamps locked_rate_cents on the new founding row from the amount the caller passes, FALLING BACK to business_monthly_cents when the caller does not know it (lib/founding/status.ts:281 and again on the update branch at :353). Those are LIFETIME terms - the rate and the marketplace take that Space keeps for good. IT CANNOT FIRE BY ACCIDENT TODAY: the grant returns no_window unless the `founding` pricing_settings row carries an explicit grace `until` date (betaGraceEndsAtMs returns null for empty), and that setting lives in production, which this container deliberately cannot read. So this is not "it is off" - it is "it is off unless you set it, and only you can see whether you did". THE DECISION IS THE OWNER'S, because it is not obviously the same question they answered. They said Business has normal pricing and only Collective gets a beta offer. But the Founding Business PROGRAM is a whole feature - badges, city caps, spots remaining - and killing its rate is not the same as declining to advertise a beta price. Either (a) set business_monthly_cents to 2900 so a Founding Business gets recognition at the normal rate, or (b) keep 1900 deliberately as a hand-granted lifetime term, the same shape as the Collective grant. Do NOT let it sit at 1900 by inattention: that is how a lifetime discount gets given away by a fallback.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const F='lib/pricing/founding.ts',K='lib/billing/pricing-keys.ts';if(!fs.existsSync(F)||!fs.existsSync(K))process.exit(79);const f=fs.readFileSync(F,'utf8');const m=/business_monthly_cents:\s*(\d+)/.exec(f);if(!m)process.exit(79);const rate=Number(m[1]);const k=fs.readFileSync(K,'utf8');const at=k.indexOf('business_base: {');if(at<0)process.exit(79);const b=/amountsFromMonthly\((\d+),\s*(\d+)\)/.exec(k.slice(at));if(!b)process.exit(79);const list=Number(b[1]),founding=Number(b[2]);if(founding!==list){console.error('business_base still carries a founding rate: '+founding+' under '+list);process.exit(1)}if(rate!==list){console.error('FOUNDING_DEFAULT.business_monthly_cents is '+rate+', not the list rate '+list+'; the beta-founder grant would stamp a lifetime discount');process.exit(1)}process.exit(0)"

entries.notes: Closed 2026-08-17. FOUNDING_DEFAULT.business_monthly_cents 1900 -> 2900. It was never a display number: grantFoundingStatus stamps it as locked_rate_cents when the caller passes no amount (lib/founding/status.ts:281 and :353), which is a LIFETIME term, so leaving it would have kept handing out a permanent $19 through a FALLBACK months after founding pricing came off every surface a customer sees. The probe asserts BOTH halves of "Business has normal pricing" - the catalog carries no founding rate AND the grant default equals the list rate - so fixing one and forgetting the other still fails. The Founding Business program is untouched: a Founding Business is now recognised at the normal rate.

entries.title: Two artifact gates exist but are not wired into postbuild, and a real build has now disproved one of them
entries.detail:
RE-STATED 2026-08-18 (ADR-1081). The row's SEQUENCING blocker is gone and its SUBSTANCE grew. The blocker was OWN-029's question about whether postbuild runs at all; a production log answered it (both prebuild and postbuild fire, and check:build-budget prints 6.04 GB across 499 functions), and vercel.json now pins buildCommand so a dashboard edit cannot take the lifecycle away. check:cache-budget was then wired in and TAKEN BACK OUT before merge. Its preview build measured 2.40 GiB raw and trimmed a 1520 MiB Turbopack cache, because the gate compares raw bytes on disk against Vercel's PACKED 1.50 GB ceiling and the two are ~2:1 apart, not the ~3% its header assumes. Its floor arm was correct (node_modules 933 MiB). The calibration is LIVE-048; this row still owns the WIRING of both gates. check:shell-weight has never printed on a completed build at all. Its one reading exited 1 naming lib/pricing/feature-meters.ts, on an artifact built plausibly BEFORE settings-panel.tsx moved five editor bodies behind dynamic(), and surface-summaries.ts mentions feature-meters only in a comment, so the failure is unconfirmed in BOTH directions. The 2026-08-17 attempt to run a real build here died collecting page data for /discover/cities/[citySlug], which needs Supabase credentials this container deliberately does not hold - but a PR's own PREVIEW BUILD runs the full postbuild and prints it, which is how check:cache-budget was caught. That is the route: wire, push, read the preview output, and only merge on green. TO CLOSE: both gates in postbuild, each landing in the same change as the preview build that printed it green.

2026-08-19, OWNER-APPROVED, HALF OF THIS IS NOW WIRED AND THE OTHER HALF IS NOT.

check:cache-budget runs in postbuild as `--warn-only`. This breaks a real deadlock rather than ignoring the rule: the ONLY thing that settles PACKED_PER_RAW is a reading from a real production artifact, and the only way to take that reading was to run on a real build. Wiring it blocking to get the reading is the 2026-08-11 incident reversed, which is what this row has always said. Warn-only is a third option that was not considered before: the script measures and prints, NEVER trims, and CANNOT exit non-zero -- not on the node_modules floor, not on its own crash. Those two guarantees are proven by MUTATION in scripts/check-cache-budget-warn-only.test.ts (8 tests): each case rewrites the script to force the condition and runs it for real, and each has a paired case asserting the same mutation DOES fail without the flag, so the guarantee cannot pass for the wrong reason. A structural arm also asserts the trim stays chained behind the warn-only branch, so no path leads from --warn-only to an rmSync.

A swallowed crash still gets a gate that notices it fired: the handler prints a 🔴 line naming the file and LIVE-035, so a broken measurement reads as broken rather than as absent.

⚠️ WARN-ONLY IS A STAGE, NOT A DESTINATION, and the same test locks that in. Its last assertion fails if postbuild ever invokes the script without --warn-only, so promoting it to blocking is a deliberate, reviewable line in a diff rather than a quiet edit to a package.json string. Promote it in the SAME change as the green build whose 'Uploading build cache [N GB]' line confirms the constant.

check:shell-weight is UNCHANGED and still unwired. Its one reading exited 1 naming lib/pricing/feature-meters.ts on an artifact built plausibly before five editor bodies moved behind dynamic(), so it is unconfirmed in BOTH directions and has no warn-only equivalent yet. This row closes when shell-weight is settled and cache-budget is promoted to blocking.

2026-08-19, SECOND HALF WIRED, SAME WAY AND FOR A SHARPER REASON. check:shell-weight now runs in postbuild as `--warn-only` alongside check:cache-budget. Its case for the stage is stronger than its sibling's: it has ONE reading in its whole life and that reading is unconfirmed in BOTH directions -- it exited 1 naming lib/pricing/feature-meters.ts on an artifact built plausibly BEFORE settings-panel.tsx moved five editor bodies behind dynamic(). So the first real thing it does may well be to report a leak, and blocking on that would fail a production deploy over a number nobody has verified.

In warn-only it measures, prints, and cannot exit non-zero: not on the byte budget, not on the fingerprint arm, not on a missing manifest, not on its own crash. Every failure path now routes through a single bail() helper, and scripts/check-shell-weight-warn-only.test.ts proves it by MUTATION -- each case forces the condition and runs the script for real, paired with a case asserting the same condition DOES fail without the flag.

🔴 THAT TEST CAUGHT A REAL HOLE WHILE IT WAS BEING WRITTEN, which is the whole argument for writing it. The uncaughtException handler was first placed next to fail(), two thirds down the file, so anything throwing during module evaluation before that point escaped it and exited 1 -- in postbuild, a dead deploy. The handler moved above all top-level work, and BOTH warn-only gates now assert that ordering, because the guarantee IS the ordering. check:cache-budget was checked for the same defect and was already safe.

scripts/check-shell-weight.test.ts carried an assertion that the gate was NOT in postbuild. It failed on this change, correctly, and was INVERTED rather than relaxed: the gate must now be present AND carry the flag, must not appear in the CI guards array, and must no longer be declared UNWIRED. Two files that cannot disagree about its state.

WHAT REMAINS FOR THIS ROW: both gates are measuring and neither can act. It closes when both are promoted to blocking, each in the same change as the green build that confirms its numbers. check:cache-budget's number is already confirmed on three builds (LIVE-048); check:shell-weight has not printed on a real artifact yet, and the first postbuild run after this merges is the one to read.

⚠️ AND THIS ROW'S PROBE HAD THE SAME DEFECT LIVE-029'S DID, found the same day on the same change. It asked only whether postbuild MENTIONS both gates. Wiring them warn-only made that true while the row stayed true, because a gate that measures and cannot act is not wired in the sense this row means. That is twice in one day that a probe measured PRESENCE where the row was about CONSEQUENCE -- the shape-not-truth failure four ADRs name, and evidently the easiest one to write by accident. Rewritten to require both gates present AND neither carrying --warn-only, so it agrees with the row today and passes only when an artifact regression can actually be stopped.

✅ THE FIX IS PROVEN, ON THE BUILD THAT SHIPPED IT. Preview deploy xpkMNeSxJCWTTn35uvCeoacVbM7n, 2026-08-19T17:05:44Z, PR #2183 -- the first artifact built with the chunk-root fix, and the first time check:shell-weight has produced an honest reading in its life:

       scanning 573 built chunk(s) under static/immutable/chunks; shell set = 21 chunk(s).
    ✅ check:shell-weight -- the shell's eager first-load JS is 1010 KB across 21 chunks,
       under the 1400 KB budget.
       8 admin module bodies checked, all lazy; read 494 client-reference manifests;
       positive control present.

EVERY PART OF THE DIAGNOSIS HELD. The root really is static/immutable/chunks (the deployment adapter's supportsImmutableAssets), which is why the old hardcoded static/chunks glob matched nothing; 573 chunks are now scanned where zero were before. The literal that the previous build said 'appears in NO built chunk' is present -- 'positive control present' plus all 8 module bodies resolving to `lazy` rather than `absent` is Arm B making a real distinction for the first time. It was never a Turbopack transform and never an unreachable module: it was the scan.

⚠️ ARM A'S FIRST REAL NUMBER IS 1010 KB, NOT 957 KB. The 957 figure (2026-08-17) came from a local build and is superseded. 1010 KB against the 1400 KB ceiling is 72% consumed, 390 KB clear, across 21 chunks rather than the 20 previously assumed. Nothing regressed -- this is the first measurement taken on the artifact users actually download, so it replaces the estimate rather than contradicting it.

🔴 THE PROMOTION CONDITION FOR check:shell-weight IS NOW MET, and it is the owner's call. AGENTS.md says wire a gate in the same change as the green build that proves it. That build exists: both arms measured, both meaningful, 28% headroom, and a superset check that fails loudly if the chunk directory ever moves again. Dropping --warn-only from the shell-weight half of postbuild is a one-token change. check:cache-budget is NOT in the same position and must not be promoted with it -- its action is a TRIM that has killed two builds, and production sits at 8.7% clear (LIVE-029), which is the closest that gate has ever been to firing.

── 2026-08-19, SHELL-WEIGHT PROMOTED, owner verbatim: "promote it." check:shell-weight runs in postbuild WITHOUT --warn-only from this change on. The promotion condition was met the honest way: it printed green on TWO PRODUCTION artifacts nobody had to squint at (17:14Z and 18:13Z deploys, both: 1010 KB eager first-load across 21 chunks under the 1400 KB budget, 8 admin module bodies all lazy, 494 manifests read, positive control present). check:cache-budget deliberately stays --warn-only: its action is a TRIM, it has killed two builds proving its own defects, and warn-only is what settled PACKED_PER_RAW=0.53 to under 1% on two production builds. Its promotion is a separate decision. The probe below still fails on that half, which is correct: this row stays open until the cache gate's promotion is decided, and the probe message now says which half is which.

── CLOSED 2026-08-19: both artifact gates now run BLOCKING in postbuild. check:shell-weight promoted 2026-08-19 (owner: "promote it") after two green production readings; check:cache-budget promoted the same day (owner: "implement best practice") after its warn-only stage settled PACKED_PER_RAW on a real build. Each promotion landed in the same change as the green build that proved it, and each warn-only pin inverted so a re-added flag fails as a silent demotion.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const P='package.json';if(!fs.existsSync(P)||!fs.existsSync('scripts/check-shell-weight.mjs')||!fs.existsSync('scripts/check-cache-budget.mjs'))process.exit(79);const pb=(JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(P,'utf8')).scripts||{}).postbuild||'';if(!pb)process.exit(79);const bad=[];for(const g of ['check-shell-weight','check-cache-budget']){const m=new RegExp(g+'\\.mjs([^&|;]*)').exec(pb);if(!m){bad.push(g+' is not in postbuild, so nothing measures it on a real build');continue}if(/--warn-only/.test(m[1]))bad.push(g+' runs in postbuild but in --warn-only mode, so it REPORTS and cannot ACT');}if(bad.length){console.error(bad.join('; ')+'. Presence is not enforcement.');process.exit(1)}process.exit(0)"

entries.notes: The probe is deliberately the CONSEQUENCE and not the intent: it fails while the two scripts are absent from postbuild and passes the moment they are wired in, so closing this row requires the wiring rather than a note saying it was considered. It exits 79 if either script is missing or postbuild is unreadable, so a reshaped package.json reports "cannot tell" instead of a clean sweep of nothing. UPDATE 2026-08-18: check:shell-weight now runs cleanly against a real (if incomplete) build in this container - 947 KB across 20 chunks, 494 client-reference manifests read, positive control present. The build still cannot COMPLETE here (page-data collection needs service-role credentials), so the postbuild wiring still waits on one green production build.

entries.title: The viewport bucket is normalized, posted, and then dropped on write
entries.detail: Found while writing the vitals route test (LIVE-030), not by looking for it. lib/analytics/vitals.ts exports vitalProps() and its comment says the sink reads the wire shape from it, but app/api/vitals/route.ts builds the props bag INLINE and omits `vp` - the viewport bucket (Lift 7d, ADR-922). So the bucket is computed on the client, posted over the wire, and then silently dropped on write: it never reaches interaction_events, and every query that would segment Core Web Vitals by viewport returns nothing. Nothing fails, which is why it survived. NOT FIXED IN THAT PASS DELIBERATELY: editing the route invalidates its digest in scripts/authz-route-ledger.json, which forces a re-read of the handler's authorization verdict, and that is a separate act from a field fix. The test asserts a SUBSET of allowed prop keys rather than an exact list, so it stays green when the fix lands and still fails if a person-level key is ever added.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const R='app/api/vitals/route.ts',V='lib/analytics/vitals.ts';if(!fs.existsSync(R)||!fs.existsSync(V))process.exit(79);const r=fs.readFileSync(R,'utf8'),v=fs.readFileSync(V,'utf8');const bad=[];const i=v.indexOf('export function vitalProps');if(i<0)process.exit(79);const body=v.slice(i,v.indexOf(String.fromCharCode(10)+'}',i));if(body.indexOf('.vp')<0&&body.indexOf('vp:')<0)bad.push('vitalProps no longer emits vp, the viewport bucket');if(r.indexOf('props: vitalProps(')<0)bad.push('the vitals route builds its own props bag again instead of calling vitalProps; that duplication is what dropped vp on write');if(bad.length){console.error(bad.join('; '));process.exit(1)}process.exit(0)"

entries.notes: Closed 2026-08-17. The route now writes props: vitalProps(v) instead of a second copy of the same object literal, so the wire shape and the written shape cannot drift again - which is the actual cause, not the missing field. MY FIRST PROBE WAS WRONG IN AN INSTRUCTIVE WAY: it looked for 'vp' near the route's `props:` literal, so it kept failing AFTER the fix, because the fix DELETED the literal it was reading. A probe written against the broken shape can outlive the break. It now asserts the two things that must both hold - vitalProps still emits vp, and the route still calls it rather than hand-rolling the bag. The authz digest was re-recorded, not bypassed: editing the handler invalidated it by design, so the `public` verdict was re-read. Nothing about the boundary moved (no session, no headers or cookies, profile_id NULL on every row whatever the payload claims, which the route test asserts with an attacker-shaped body), and vp is a property of the PAGE VIEW rather than the person (ADR-922).

entries.title: Two eyebrow registers exist and neither is wrong: pick the one that wins
entries.detail: Surfaced by LIVE-025, and it is a design decision rather than a refactor, which is why it is not being made in code. There are TWO eyebrow implementations and nobody reconciled them. (1) app/globals.css locks the `eyebrow` utility at 0.75rem / 0.18em / bold, and 87 sites use it. (2) components/page-editor/blocks/kit.tsx exports an <Eyebrow> component with about 26 adopters rendering text-body-sm, 0.875rem - which is DAWN's DECLARED eyebrow size, i.e. precisely the half of the DAWN split that globals.css resolved DOWN to 0.75rem on 2026-08-05. So the block kit is not drifting by accident; it is rendering the value DAWN published, and the CSS is rendering the value this repo chose instead. Beyond those two there is a third de-facto register: 615 sites pair uppercase with a literal tracking, dominated by an 11px `text-2xs font-semibold uppercase tracking-wide text-muted`, and many of those are pill badges and dense table headers where 0.18em would widen the label past the pill that was sized to fit it. THE CALL: which size is the eyebrow - 0.75rem (globals.css, what most of the kit uses) or 0.875rem (DAWN's declaration, what the block kit renders)? Whichever loses gets retired, and its adopters move in a bounded sweep with a visual recapture. Deciding it also settles what goes back to DAWN in the next handoff, since design_handoff/PROD-AHEAD.md already carries the divergence.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const K='components/page-editor/blocks/kit.tsx',T='lib/theme/eyebrow-role.test.ts';if(!fs.existsSync(K)||!fs.existsSync(T))process.exit(79);const k=fs.readFileSync(K,'utf8'),t=fs.readFileSync(T,'utf8');if(k.indexOf('Eyebrow')<0)process.exit(79);const bad=[];const code=k.split(String.fromCharCode(10)).filter(function(x){var s=x.trim();return s.indexOf('//')!==0&&s.indexOf('*')!==0}).join(String.fromCharCode(10));if(code.indexOf('text-body-sm')>=0)bad.push('the block kit declares text-body-sm again: the retired 0.875rem eyebrow register is back');if(t.indexOf('composes the role in the atom')<0)bad.push('the assertion that the atom may not restate the role is gone from '+T);if(t.indexOf('never pairs the block-kit marker with the retired')<0)bad.push('the retired-size assertion is gone from '+T);if(bad.length){console.error(bad.join('; '));process.exit(1)}process.exit(0)"

entries.notes: DECIDED AND IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-18 (ADR-1075). Owner's call: 0.75rem wins. The block kit's <Eyebrow> atom now COMPOSES the `eyebrow` utility and declares none of the role, so an adopter can no longer pick a size by choosing an import. The framing worth keeping is the ADR's: the eyebrow had two implementations because it had two OWNERS, a class and an import. globals.css locked 0.75rem; the atom hand-rolled the same role at text-body-sm, 0.875rem - DAWN's DECLARED size, and precisely the half of DAWN's own split this repo resolved down on 2026-08-05. Two registers 17% apart and NEITHER was a mistake, which is exactly why it needed a decision rather than a refactor. Verified by breaking it, not on report: reintroducing 'text-body-sm font-bold uppercase tracking-eyebrow' inside the atom fails with 'the <Eyebrow> atom restates the role', and restoring goes green. Three assertions hold it, including a non-vacuity arm so a green over an empty scan is not a pass. The 608 literal-tracking sites are deliberately untouched and stay a ratchet: genuine eyebrows sit beside pill badges and dense table headers where 0.18em would widen a label past the pill it was sized to fit.

entries.title: Ten more client entry points still drag the service-role client into the browser graph
entries.detail: LIVE-009 fixed two instances and revealed the CLASS. lib/supabase/admin.ts is still statically reachable in the client layer from ten other 'use client' entry points, every one the same shape: a client component imports a constant or a small helper out of a module that also opens the service-role client, and the whole graph follows. The paths are via lib/crm/relationships, lib/crm/contacts-roster, lib/crm/pipeline, lib/personas, lib/walkthroughs, lib/billing/tips, lib/spaces/membership, lib/marketplace, lib/season-ranks -> lib/quest/completion-read, and lib/events/event-stats. THE FIX IS THE ONE LIVE-009 USED, and it is small per instance: extract the leaf the client actually needs into a dependency-free module, re-export it from the old home so no server caller changes, then put a real `import 'server-only'` on the original so the class FAILS THE BUILD instead of being re-litigated. The header comment saying 'Server-only' is what both LIVE-009 files had, and it stopped nothing. Worth doing in batches with a build between them, because `server-only` fails at compile and the failure names the importer, so each batch is self-diagnosing.

verify.cmd: node scripts/check-client-server-boundary.mjs --probe

entries.notes: BATCH ONE DONE 2026-08-18: the three CRM paths are cut (relationships, contacts-roster, pipeline). BATCH TWO DONE 2026-08-18, and it closes the row: the remaining seven are cut the same way - the pure leaf the client actually needs moved to a dependency-free module (personas-core, walkthroughs-core, tips-core, membership-core, marketplace-core, event-stats-core), re-exported from its old home so no server caller changed, and the original took `import 'server-only'`. TWO OF THE TEN WERE NOT THE WORK THE ROW DESCRIBED. (1) lib/season-ranks.ts must NOT take the directive: it is pure rank vocabulary that ~20 client components import, including lib/community-roles which app-shell.tsx pulls onto every route under app/(main). Its ONLY impurity was one convenience re-export of journeysFinishedThisSeason; the fix was to REMOVE that line and guard lib/quest/completion-read.ts instead, repointing five server callers. Adding `server-only` to season-ranks - which the old probe demanded - would have broken the build. (2) An ELEVENTH path the row never listed: composer-shell.tsx -> lib/spaces/email-topics -> lib/comms/contact-preferences -> admin, for one constant; extracted to lib/comms/contact-topics.ts. 🔴 THE PROBE WAS REPLACED, NOT WIDENED. A hand-kept list of ten measured a subset and reported on the whole - the same instrument failure as batch one's, one level up - and it also PRESCRIBED A REMEDY (`server-only` in each named file) rather than measuring a consequence, which is how it came to demand the wrong fix for season-ranks. The row now probes scripts/check-client-server-boundary.mjs: it walks the real import graph and fails if ANY 'use client' module can statically reach lib/supabase/admin.ts, with no baseline and no allowlist. It is wired into the ci.yml guard array as check:client-boundary (guard-wiring.test.ts would have failed otherwise). PROVEN TO FIRE both ways before commit: repointing tip-button.tsx back at lib/billing/tips reported the server-only violation, and additionally stripping the directive reported the full path through to the admin client; restoring both returned it to green. It counts STATIC edges only: a dynamic `await import()` is a separate chunk and is this repo's deliberate, documented mitigation in page-chrome.ts and apps/overrides.ts. Counting those called 47 entry points where 20 were real, so they are printed as a note and never fail.

entries.title: The retired 0.875rem eyebrow stopped rendering: 25 sites moved onto the role, one named carve-out left

source.ref: OWN-027 / ADR-1075; ADR-1072 section 2 for the one carve-out

entries.detail: CLOSED 2026-08-18. 25 sites across 12 files moved off `text-body-sm font-bold uppercase tracking-eyebrow` and onto the `eyebrow` utility, which is the whole role in one class: 0.75rem, 0.18em, bold, uppercase, grotesk. That is the size the owner chose in ADR-1075 and it is the size the block kit's atom has composed since the same day; until now a visitor saw two eyebrow sizes on the same marketing page depending on whether a section came from a block or from the route file. TWO SITES DELIBERATELY DO NOT MOVE, and they are different cases. components/page-editor/blocks/spaces.tsx is a photo-hero whose eyebrow sits on text-on-ink/80 over an image - ADR-1072 section 2's named carve-out, and the only thing left of it. components/templates/page-hero.tsx line 276 was ALREADY 0.75rem at base (text-meta) and only its `sm:text-body-sm` step-up was the retired register, so dropping the step-up completes the retirement; moving it to the composite would additionally change font-family and line-height, which this row never asked for. THE ADOPTION RATCHET DOES NOT MOVE, and that is correct rather than a miss: handrolled-eyebrow counts uppercase paired with a LITERAL tracking (tracking-wide/wider/widest or an arbitrary em). Every site swept here used tracking-eyebrow, the token, so none of them was ever in that population. Its 608 is the separate heterogeneous population the ratchet exists to hold. lib/theme/eyebrow-role.test.ts kept a comment justifying the token-only form by saying 'the marketing register sets the same role at --text-body-sm over a photograph'. That sentence was true when written and describes one file now, so it was corrected in the same pass rather than left to read as a live register. THE VISUAL BASELINES MOVE, which is why the row carried a scope warning: this is a real size change on every captured marketing surface. Recaptured in this PR via the e2e (manual) workflow against the PR's own preview URL, and verified by pr-compare on the following push.

entries.title: One dropped TCP connection during prerender kills the whole deploy, and nothing retries
entries.detail: OBSERVED, not theorised. The preview build of 656dac3 failed while the PRODUCTION build of the SAME COMMIT succeeded four minutes earlier. The failure: `TypeError: fetch failed / Caused by: Error: read ECONNRESET` on a Supabase read, which the reader wraps as DiscoverReadError and rethrows, and Next reports 'Export encountered an error on /discover/events/[slug]/page: breathe-connect-expand-2026-09-10, exiting the build.' One transient reset on one slug ended the export. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ONE FLAKY PREVIEW: `main` is protected and MERGING DEPLOYS TO PRODUCTION (AGENTS.md). This same read runs during the production export, so the same blip takes down a production deploy, and the only evidence would be a stack trace that looks like a code fault. The build is otherwise healthy - the report says 'No memory or disk space problems detected'. THE FIX IS NOT A BARE try/catch. Swallowing the error would silently ship a /discover with missing events, which is the fail-safe-with-no-gate pattern AGENTS.md names ('every fail-safe needs a gate that notices it fired'). The honest shape is a bounded retry with backoff around the read for RETRYABLE transport faults only (ECONNRESET, ETIMEDOUT, fetch failed), leaving a genuine query error - bad SQL, RLS denial, missing column - fatal exactly as it is now. If a retry is exhausted the build should still fail, loudly, with the slug named. A count of retries consumed belongs in the build log so a rising number is visible before it becomes an outage.

entries.notes: DONE 2026-08-18. The discover read seam (lib/discover.ts listRead/detailRead) now retries TRANSIENT failures twice with 250/500ms backoff. The observed killer arrived RESOLVED, not thrown - supabase-js catches the fetch rejection and resolves with a synthetic error whose message carries the network cause - so the retry decision reads the error's SHAPE: network-ish (fetch failed/ECONNRESET/ETIMEDOUT/EAI_AGAIN/...) retries, a Postgres/PostgREST code never does, and empty data is NEVER retried (a detail-route empty result is a believed 404; retry-until-it-exists turns 404s into timeouts). Call sites pass thunks so each attempt builds a fresh PostgrestBuilder - re-awaiting one builder re-reads its settled failure. lib/discover.test.ts proves the retry FIRES (two transient failures then success = three calls) and REFUSES (deterministic error = one call), per the watch-it-fail rule.

entries.title: /the-lab and /the-community emit no FAQPage, and have not since their templates landed
entries.detail:
Found while retiring the-lab's coded body, and it is NOT caused by that retirement. THE_LAB_FAQ carried five Q&A and its faqSchema() call sat on the LEGACY branch of `data ? <BlockRender/> : <Legacy/>` - the branch that could never be taken, because the template is a static literal and `data` is never null. So /the-lab has emitted no FAQPage structured data since the template landed. The retirement deleted the source copy; it did not change what Google sees, which was already nothing. MEASURED, and NARROWER THAN FIRST REPORTED: lib/page-editor/templates/the-quest.ts contains 1 Accordion block and the-lab.ts contains 0. the-quest is therefore FINE - its Accordion emits the FAQPage through BlockDocJsonLd, exactly as its own code comment says. This row is /the-lab alone. THE FIX IS A CONTENT DECISION, not a schema patch: adding faqSchema back without visible Q&A on the page would assert markup for copy a visitor cannot see, which CONTENT-VOICE section 8b forbids and Google penalises. The honest fix is an Accordion block in the-lab's template carrying the five questions, which emits the FAQPage as a consequence of rendering them. That MOVES PIXELS on /the-lab across four skins and two viewports, so it needs a baseline recapture in the same PR. The five drafted answers are good and are preserved in git history at the retirement commit.

── RE-MEASURED 2026-08-19 in a premise sweep (ADR-1082), and it HOLDS. Confirmed against PRODUCTION HTML rather than the tree: https://frequencylocal.com/the-lab serves 6 application/ld+json blocks (Article, BreadcrumbList, WebPage, WebSite, Organization, Place, ImageObject) and ZERO FAQPage. lib/page-editor/templates/the-lab.ts still holds 0 Accordion blocks; the-quest.ts holds one. The premise is confirmed live, not merely in source. Still blocked on the visual baseline recapture, which needs VERCEL_AUTOMATION_BYPASS_SECRET.

── RE-AUDITED 2026-08-19 and the 'this row is /the-lab alone' conclusion is WRONG. /the-community has the identical defect: lib/page-editor/templates/the-community.ts carries ZERO Accordion blocks, and in app/(marketing)/the-community/page.tsx its faqSchema(COMMUNITY_FAQ) call sits on the same unreachable legacy branch, because getTemplate('the-community') is a static literal and `data` is never null. The template file SAYS SO ITSELF ('The FAQPage is deliberately NOT emitted here: this template contains no Accordion'), in a comment that landed 2026-08-13, six days before the re-measure that concluded /the-lab alone. Also corrected: the-quest.ts carries THREE Accordion blocks, not one. Source-confirmed only for /the-community (this session's egress to frequencylocal.com is blocked); /the-lab was confirmed against live HTML.

THE OLD PROBE WAS A WORD SEARCH. It passed on the string 'Accordion' appearing in the template, which an Accordion with zero items also satisfies while the page still emits nothing: the block filters out any pair missing an answer. It now requires a question/answer pair in BOTH templates.

── CODE HALF DONE 2026-08-19. Both templates now carry an Accordion whose visible Q&A emit the FAQPage (CONTENT-VOICE 8b). /the-lab: the five THE_LAB_FAQ Q&A recovered VERBATIM from the retirement commit's parent (c3228d76c^) into tl-faq, placed between the PhotoTrio and the PillarNav, mirroring the-quest. /the-community: FOUR of COMMUNITY_FAQ's five recovered verbatim into tc-faq (before the ink close); the cost answer was NOT carried forward: 'The personal tier, Crew, is ${CREW_NOTE.foundingLabel} a month' quotes the pay-what-you-want FLOOR as a fixed price, which the CREW_NOTE contract forbids (every surface must read as 'from'); flagged for the owner rather than rewritten. The dead faqSchema(COMMUNITY_FAQ) call on the route's unreachable legacy branch was deleted (getTemplate is a static well-formed literal, data is never null); the rest of that rung is LIVE-006's work. the-lab.test.ts and the-community.test.ts assert one Accordion, all pairs well-formed under the block's own filter, and the recovered questions verbatim. REMAINS before close: pixels move on both routes across four skins and two viewports, so the visual-baseline recapture (needs VERCEL_AUTOMATION_BYPASS_SECRET, dispatched in CI after this lands) plus a look at the rendered pages. THE PROBE NOW MEASURES BOTH HALVES: with the Accordion landed, the old Q&A-only probe passed while the row stayed open, which check-backlog rightly calls a contradiction, and the fix the gate itself names is correcting a probe that proves the wrong thing. It still requires the Accordion q/a pairs, and now also that each route's 8 committed baselines under test/e2e/__screenshots__/visual.spec.ts are no older than the template (a dirty template with clean baselines, or baselines whose last commit predates the template's, fails with 'recapture needed'). The probe goes green in the recapture commit, which is when this row closes.

── PROBE HARDENED 2026-08-19: CI checks out depth=1, where every file's last commit is HEAD, so the baseline-freshness half passed vacuously and the open row read as done. A shallow clone now reports indeterminate (exit 79) instead of a fake verdict; the freshness half is enforced wherever real history exists.

── RE-MEASURED 2026-08-20 (emboss capture, PR #2196): HALF TRUE IN PRODUCTION. /the-lab renders the accordion (its 8 visual baselines changed and its FAQPage emits — the route serves the CODE TEMPLATE because its pages row is an unpublished draft). /the-community does NOT: the live page serves a PUBLISHED pages row from 2026-07-13 (13 blocks, owner-authored in the editor), which wins over the template by design (lib/page-editor/data.ts), so #2190's accordion never reached that route. Completing this row on /the-community means adding the 4-question Accordion block to the OWNER'S published document (or the owner publishing it from the editor) — a content edit to an owner-authored live page, so it is the owner's call, asked 2026-08-20. The freshness probe stays honestly red on the-community until then.

The /the-community blocker was the owner-published pages row that shadowed the code template; this session confirmed that row was a corrupted verbatim template-copy (identical 13 block types/ids, no SEO overrides) and DELETED it, so the route now serves the code template (the-community.ts) with its tc-faq Accordion, exactly like /the-lab. The #2209 capture (runner commit af3d9426e) recaptured all 8 the-community visual baselines; /the-lab's landed with #2196. Probe exits 0 against full history (both templates carry an Accordion with q/a pairs, both routes serve the template, both baseline sets are newer than their template commits).
